answer: Standing starts only after a bond is posted at an isolated tundra checkpoint whose site and audit hour are revealed after lock, so a farm cannot pre-stage one operator at every post. Weight moves only along a pre-declared river of time-locked waypoints, one release per epoch; a second key that shares a payer, host, or travel clock is fused and the bond burns. A public trellis of those waypoints must collect three independent crossings before any vote counts, and a missed crossing or later identity-fuse cuts the lattice and slashes the stake, so extra names cost more than they return.
